title: Salvenkirchlein Chapel on the Hohe Salve
name: Salvenkirchlein Chapel on the Hohe Salve
kurzbeschreibung: The Salvenkirchlein on the Hohe Salve at 1,829 m: Austria's highest pilgrimage church with a 360-degree panoramic view of over 70 three-thousand-metre peaks.
beschreibung:
Overview

The visible-from-afar Salvenkirchlein (officially the pilgrimage church of St. Johannes der Täufer) perches directly atop the dome-shaped summit of the famous Hohe Salve at an altitude of 1,829 metres above sea level. Located on the border of the Tyrolean districts of Kitzbühel and Kufstein between Hopfgarten and Söll, this small baroque house of worship is considered the highest pilgrimage church in all of Austria. Due to its freestanding, solitary position, the Hohe Salve provides one of the most stunning mountain panoramas in Europe, featuring unobstructed 360-degree vistas of more than 70 glaciated three-thousand-metre peaks across the Hohe Tauern and Zillertaler Alpen.

Pilgrimage History & Sundials

The origins of the pilgrimage date back at least to the year 1589, when a summit chapel was first recorded in historical documents. Legend has it that the church was built as a sanctuary against severe summer thunderstorms; to this day, John the Baptist is revered here as a powerful patron saint of weather. Following destruction by lightning, today's baroque church with its onion dome and solid shingle walls was erected in 1665 to withstand extreme alpine weather. Inside, visitors admire a magnificent baroque high altar and historic votive paintings. Surrounding the church, the fascinating Sonnenuhrenweg (Sundial Trail) has been established: 15 artistic timekeeping stations and a walk-in wind harp illustrate the secrets of the sun's trajectory and alpine weather phenomena.

Visit & Getting There

During the operating seasons of the mountain cable cars from late May to late October, the Salvenkirchlein is open during daytime and free of charge for visits and prayer. Accessibility: The Hohe Salve can be reached comfortably from two sides via modern gondolas – with the Salvenbahn from Hopfgarten or with the cable cars from Söll (via Hexenwasser). Mountain lift fare round trip (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €32.00, children approx. €16.00. Holders of the SkiWelt Erlebnis-Wanderpass ride free of charge. Arriving by car: Via the B170 to Hopfgarten or B178 to Söll (large free parking lots at the valley stations). By public transport: ÖBB train to Hopfgarten Berglift station, just a few steps from the valley station.

Tips

From the mountain station of the gondola, a paved, stepless panoramic path leads in just two minutes on foot directly to the church and the viewing platform (wheelchair accessible). Stop by the adjacent Gipfelalm Hohe Salve – on Austria's first rotating panoramic terrace, the 360-degree mountain scenery slowly glides past while you enjoy your Tyrolean snack.
